text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnian Prime Minister Hasan Muratovic criticizes an interview that U.S. envoy Richard Sklar gave to Oslobodjenje on Wednesday. In the interview Sklar accused Bosnian government of moving slowly towards market economy and democracy.
- Bosnian ambassador to Croatia reacts to speculation that Croatia will ask for certain changes along the border with Bosnia. "Bosnian Parliament is in charge of these isues".
- Croat and Moslem officials of Neretva canton failed to name a head of local police. Croats ask for International Police Task force to appoint its representative for this post.
- Main Bosnian Moslem party, SDA, says it will attend the Bosnian Serb national assembly session on Saturday if the text of a solemn oath is changed.
- "Dayton accord has to be revised in aspects of monetary and social policy" Bosnian minister without portfolio Dragoljub Stojanov says in an interview.

- The main Moslem party, SDA, asks for local elections in Brcko to be delayed as long as process of arbitration is not carried out to resolve territorial dispute. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864. REUTER SS/SC
